laws.rule: Jail for possession of any quantity of illegal drugs.
Sabbath laws strictly limit Sunday activity, including work unless exempt, sport, loud music and fishing. Public exercise and swimming on Sunday are frowned on and can draw police.
It is illegal for anyone over 6 to bare the top half of the body in public. Outside hotels, people swim in rash vests or t-shirts. Topless bathing is not accepted.
Legal drinking age 18. Drink-driving limit about 0.05 BAC with roadside testing; drinking in a vehicle can be penalised.
Drive on an Australian licence for up to 12 months, then a local licence through the Ministry of Infrastructure. Don't leave the scene of an accident until police say so.

culture-and-protocol.dress_and_conduct: A highly religious, mostly Christian, conservative country. Show respect for the Royal Family. Dress modestly and avoid public affection; modest swimwear at public beaches. Tonga Tourism: under the Sunday law, most work, sport and trading stop. Cover shoulders and knees in villages and at church. Going topless in public is illegal, and men shouldn't go shirtless away from resorts.
culture-and-protocol.cultural_authority: Ask locally: your host, church or village.

items.text: Tonga has strict rules on drugs.
You can go to jail for possession of any quantity of illegal drugs.
This includes if you are carrying drugs.
The legal blood alcohol limit for drivers is 250 micrograms of alcohol per litre of breath, which is equivalent to a blood alcohol concentration (BAC) of around 0.05%.
Penalties vary depending on the recorded alcohol level and may include fines, court proceedings, and, in more serious cases, imprisonment.
Passengers should also be aware that consuming alcohol in a vehicle may attract penalties under local laws.
